title: Space stock sell-off isn't about fundamentals, it's about spacex and overvaluation (imo)
author: linabell-631
selftext:
okay so, watching the space sector absolutely bleed out today and it's kinda wild. like, everyone's panicking but i really think this isn't some fundamental shift, you know? it's all about spacex. that ipo is gonna be HUGE, probably one of the biggest ever, and people need cash to get in on it. so what do they do? they sell off their existing space holdings. it's just a capital rotation, not a sign that suddenly all these companies suck. i mean, look at spcx today, up another 8.7% and like 40% over five sessions. that's exactly the inverse of what's happening to the small caps. tells ya everything right there.

and honestly, these valuations were stretched to begin with. like, PL up 410% in a year, RKLB almost 300%... most of these aren't even profitable yet! RKLB is still like 80x sales even after this drop. ASTS has basically no revenue but a multi-billion dollar market cap. it was just a matter of time before something lit the fuse, and the spacex drain was it. high-multiple growth stocks always get hit hardest when sentiment turns, it's just how it goes. 



plus, spacex going public is gonna be a massive re-pricing benchmark. suddenly you have this giant, super well-funded, vertically integrated company on the market, and investors are gonna compare everyone else to it. it's kinda ironic that some of these companies, like ASTS, even rely on spacex to launch their own stuff. your competitor is also your supplier, wild.



i still think the long-term thesis for space is solid, like ai infra, it's a structural growth thing. but this isn't a "buy the dip blindly" moment. this is a "reassess everything" moment. these stocks aren't cheap now, they just went from ridiculously overvalued to merely expensive. i'm not buying anything yet. if you're holding, and your thesis is long-term, probably just ride it out. but if you're in some of the more speculative stuff like ASTS or PL, maybe take a look at your margin of error. rklb seems the most solid, but still pricey. just my two cents, what do you guys think?

  
(\*reference only, not investment advice)
